name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
summary: A walking, single-leg movement with dumbbells that trains the quads and glutes while challenging balance and coordination.
setup: Pick up a dumbbell in each hand and hold them at your sides.
Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart and brace your trunk.
Clear a lane about 10 to 15 steps long.
execution: Take a long step forward and plant your whole foot.
Lower straight down until your back knee approaches the floor and the front thigh is about parallel.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee in line with your toes.
Push through the front foot to stand up and bring the back leg forward into the next step.
Alternate legs and walk the lane, turning around to return if needed.
mistakes: Taking steps that are too short so the front knee runs far past the toes: take a longer stride.
Leaning forward: keep your chest up and the dumbbells at your sides.
Knee collapsing inward: push the front knee out in line with the toes.
Rushing and losing balance: slow the pace and lighten the dumbbells.

references.title: Master Your Dumbbell Walking Lunges: Avoid Common Mistakes For Stronger Legs | J2FIT
references.author: Mike | J2FIT Strength & Conditioning
